Issues.Title: DomainUpDown/NumericUpDown size and location cannot be restored after changing and resetting Font
Issues.Body:
### .NET version

.NET 11 SDK build: 11.0.100

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Yes

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

No, also repro in .NET 8

### Issue description

After changing and resetting the Form's Font, changing the Font of a DomainUpDown or NumericUpDown control causes the control's size and/or location to change unexpectedly in the WinForms Designer.

After resetting the control's Font, the control does not return to its original size and location. Using Undo also does not restore the original layout.

The issue reproduces with both DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6c3235f-dc92-49f2-82b9-ffdd8803506d


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a WinForms application.
2. Add a DomainUpDown and a NumericUpDown control to the Form.
3. Change the Form's Font to a different font or font size.
4. Reset the Form's Font.
5. Change the Font of the DomainUpDown or NumericUpDown control.
6. Observe the control's size and location.
7. Reset the control's Font.
8. Observe the control's size and location again.
9. Use Undo to try to restore the previous layout.

**Actual behavior**
After changing the control's Font:

- The control's width and/or location changes.
- Resetting the control's Font does not restore the original size and location.
- Using Undo does not restore the control to its original size and location.
As a result, the control can remain incorrectly sized or positioned in the Designer even after the Font property has been reset.

**Expected behavior**
After resetting the control's Font, the control should return to the appropriate size and position based on the original font.
Undo should also restore the control's previous size and location.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Prevent clipboard hangs during concurrent data-store access
Issues.Body:
Fixes [3084829](https://devdiv.visualstudio.com/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/3084829)

Backport of #15319 to release/11.0

/cc @Shyam-Gupta @nareshjo

## Root Cause

The clipboard data store reads, writes, and enumerates its format dictionary without synchronization. Concurrent mutation can corrupt dictionary state; on .NET Framework, a corrupted bucket chain can cause a later lookup to loop indefinitely.

## Proposed changes

- Protect the clipboard data store's format dictionary against overlapping managed calls and COM callbacks.
- Capture complete entries and coherent format snapshots while keeping validation, deserialization, and format mapping outside the per-store gate.
- Cover concurrent insertion and overwrites, callback reentrancy, format compatibility, and native storage-medium ownership with regression tests.

## Customer Impact

- The synchronization gap was identified while investigating customer-reported clipboard hangs. This change addresses a dictionary-corruption race that can cause clipboard operations to fail or hang.
- Existing format mapping and native drag-and-drop ownership behavior are preserved; no public API changes.

## Regression?

- Unconfirmed. The unsynchronized dictionary predates this change; an introducing release has not been established.

## Risk

Low expected compatibility risk. The per-store gate protects dictionary access and snapshot creation; validation, deserialization, format mapping, and explicit COM calls stay outside locked sections. Payload ownership is unchanged. Lock contention and larger snapshots add potential performance costs.

## Test methodology

- Exercise colliding concurrent insertions, concurrent reads and overwrites, complete data/flag publication, and coherent format enumeration.
- Verify validation and deserialization callbacks can wait for another thread to access the store. Check format mapping/order, validation failures, serializable first-entry behavior, and native-medium ownership.
- Rebuild the affected test project with the repository's Arcade workflow in Debug and Release. Run the final DataStore regression tests on both targets: 10 Framework cases and 11 modern .NET cases per configuration, totaling 42 passes with no failures or skips.
- Exercise the exact timeout-cleanup block in an isolated Framework harness with completed, cancellable, and delayed workers. All three checks passed; this checks cleanup behavior, not product COM contention.
- Basic copy/paste and undo smoke checks with a consumer using the same production fix completed without observed failures. The original intermittent hang has not been reproduced and verified fixed.

## Test environment(s)

- Windows x64, Debug and Release.
- .NET Framework 4.8.1 target (`net481`).
- Modern target: `net11.0-windows7.0`, executed using the repository-selected .NET runtime `12.0.0-alpha.1.26519.114`.
- Repository-local .NET SDK: `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102`.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Let each platform declare the TYMEDs it supports so WPF can provide enhanced metafiles
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/wpf#11986

## Proposed changes

- Add `IOleServices.AllowedTymeds`, following the existing `#if NET static abstract` pattern.
- `Composition` reads the allowed media types from the platform instead of the hard-coded `TYMED_HGLOBAL | TYMED_ISTREAM | TYMED_GDI`, in both the managed-to-native and native-to-managed adapters.
- `WinFormsOleServices` returns the old value, so WinForms behavior is unchanged. WPF adds `TYMED_ENHMF` in the companion PR.

## Customer Impact

- On .NET 10+, WPF apps can't provide `CF_ENHMETAFILE` to other applications: every `TYMED_ENHMF` request fails with `DV_E_TYMED` before WPF's handler runs. Pasting EMF into apps like Word fails silently, with no workaround.

## Regression?

- Yes. .NET 9 WPF allowed `TYMED_ENHMF`, and the shared mask dropped it.

## Risk

- Low. WinForms gets the same value as before, and `IOleServices` is internal.
- The value is per platform rather than added to the shared constant, because WinForms can't supply or read EMF. A shared value would make WinForms report EMF as available when it isn't.

## Test methodology

- CTI manual validation
- Added `ManagedToNativeAdapterTests`, which fails with `DV_E_TYMED` without this change.
- `System.Private.Windows.Core.Tests` passes on net11.0 and net481.
- Validated end-to-end with a WPF app on .NET 11 RC 1, using WPF built with the companion change: EMF paste now works for delayed and flushed data.

Issues.Title: Fix UpDown sizing and focus-indicator flicker with .NET 11 styles
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15323, #15324

## Root cause

Two issues affect the modern .NET 11 visual style:

1. **Design-time sizing**: Font-change handling updates the control height only for classic styles or when `AutoSize` is enabled. Since `AutoSize` defaults to false, modern controls retain their previous height in the designer, leaving the buttons unchanged.
2. **Focus-indicator flicker**: Every button press calls `Focus() `on the outer control, even when its edit control is already focused. Focus temporarily leaves the edit control and then returns, triggering unnecessary focus transitions and restarting the bottom-edge focus indicator.

## Proposed changes

- Update `DomainUpDown `and `NumericUpDown `heights when their font changes at design time, including when` AutoSize` is `false`. Resize the Up/Down buttons accordingly.
- Avoid redundant focus transfers when pressing modern Up/Down buttons while the edit control already has focus.
- Add regression tests for both controls and include them in the design-surface demo for manual verification.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Developers can change fonts in the designer and have both the control and its buttons resize to accommodate the text.
- Users can press Up/Down buttons repeatedly without unnecessary focus transitions that cause the highlighted bottom edge to flicker.

## Regression? 

- No

## Risk

- MInimal

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

- Changing the font at design time leaves the control and button heights unchanged when AutoSize is false.
- Pressing Up/Down buttons causes redundant lost-focus/got-focus transitions, making the bottom-edge highlight flicker.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e41c5511-e856-4774-bb44-c2d0520c26a1

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/658d2118-38e4-4263-9417-330e2f9ad44e

### After

- Changing the font at design time adjusts the control and button heights when increasing or decreasing the font size.
- Pressing Up/Down buttons preserves edit focus when already focused. An unfocused control still acquires focus normally.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf88e5d7-2b0a-4aac-8982-195642df0e47

## Test methodology <!-- How did you ensure quality? -->

- Manual tests and unit tests

.NET 11 SDK build: 11.0.100

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Not tested/verified

When VisualStylesMode is set to Net11, changing the Font of a DomainUpDown or NumericUpDown control in the Form Designer does not immediately update the control's height.

2. Set VisualStylesMode to Net11.

5. Observe the control height.
6. Close and reopen the Form Designer.
7. Observe the control height again.

Issues.Title: NumericUpDown/DomainUpDown flicker when rapidly clicking the Up/Down buttons with accent colors in VisualStylesMode.Net11
Issues.Body:

Not tested/verified

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

New APIs in .NET 11

When VisualStylesMode is set to Net11, the NumericUpDown/DomainUpDown control shows a visible flickering/fading effect when clicking the Up or Down button.

The behavior is clearly visible on a physical machine but has not been reproduced on a VM.

**Expected behavior**
The NumericUpDown/DomainUpDown should transition/render smoothly without visible flickering or an unintended fade-in/fade-out effect during clicking.

Issues.Title: Analyzer-specific properties in eng/Analyzer.props are evaluated before IsAnalyzerProject is set
Issues.Body:
### Issue description

Follow-up discovered while investigating dotnet/winforms#15314; separate from its architecture-routing fix.

`Directory.Build.props` imports `eng/Analyzer.props` before the project body is evaluated. `eng/Analyzer.props` defaults `IsAnalyzerProject` to `false` and immediately conditions a property group on it being `true`. However, the analyzer/code-fix projects declare `<IsAnalyzerProject>true</IsAnalyzerProject>` in their project bodies, after that import.

Consequently, the conditional group is skipped and is not reevaluated when the project later sets the property. Its intended settings do not take effect:

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(IsAnalyzerProject)' == 'true'">
  <IsRoslynComponent>true</IsRoslynComponent>
  <DefineConstants>WINFORMS_ANALYZERS</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

This means the projects are marked as analyzer projects by the end of evaluation, but lack the intended Roslyn-component marker and compilation symbol. No additional runtime or packaging failure is claimed here; the confirmed defect is the missing evaluated properties.

### Steps to reproduce

In a restored checkout, run:

```powershell
dotnet msbuild src\System.Windows.Forms.Analyzers\src\System.Windows.Forms.Analyzers.csproj -getProperty:IsAnalyzerProject,IsRoslynComponent,DefineConstants -nologo
```

Observed:

```json
{
  "Properties": {
    "IsAnalyzerProject": "true",
    "IsRoslynComponent": "",
    "DefineConstants": "TRACE;DEBUG"
  }
}
```

Expected: `IsRoslynComponent=true`, and `DefineConstants` includes `WINFORMS_ANALYZERS` while preserving existing symbols.

### Suggested scope

Apply analyzer-dependent settings after the project has declared `IsAnalyzerProject` (for example, in the existing analyzer targets mechanism), preserving any existing compilation symbols. Add evaluation regression coverage for the C# and VB analyzer/code-fix projects, plus a non-analyzer control project.

### .NET version

Reproduced with the repository-pinned SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102` during investigation of dotnet/winforms#15314.

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Not applicable: repository MSBuild evaluation issue.

### Did it work in any earlier release?

Not verified; this appears to predate the changes in dotnet/winforms#15314.

Issues.Title: Fix DataGridView losing the current cell after row removal
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15317

## Root cause

A change in #12534 discarded the replacement current-cell address returned by the row-removal preparation logic and passed an invalid address to the subsequent notification instead.

The preparation logic clears the current cell when its row is removed. Without the replacement address, the post-removal logic cannot restore the current cell and selection.


## Proposed changes

- Preserve the replacement current-cell address returned during row removal and pass it to the collection-change notification.
- Restore the existing logic that updates the current cell and selection after removing a row.
- Add five regression cases covering removal of the current first, middle, and last rows, and consecutive Delete-key operations on bound and unbound grids.


<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- This fix restores the previous behavior: the next visible row becomes current after users delete the current row, or the previous visible row when no suitable next row exists, allowing keyboard interaction to continue.


## Regression? 

- Yes 

## Risk

- Low

<!-- end TELL-MODE -->


## Screenshots <!-- Remove this section if PR does not change UI -->

### Before

Deleting the current row from a bound or unbound grid, or removing it through Rows.RemoveAt on an unbound grid, can leave CurrentCell and CurrentRow null with no row selected. Subsequent keyboard operations require manually selecting a cell.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e7c6937-940a-4029-9ec9-32d176800b1d



### After

The grid restores the current cell and selection to the appropriate remaining row. The current column is preserved, and consecutive Delete-key operations continue to work.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a760df69-cb8e-487c-abd5-359a14e324bd

- Unit tests and manual tests

Issues.Title: Keep single-instance forwarding alive after a StartupNextInstance exception
Issues.Body: Fixes #15316 Related to #14973 ## Root Cause The listener for new launches dispatches the handler with synchronous `Control.Invoke` through `WindowsFormsApplicationBase.OnStartupNextInstanceMarshallingAdaptor`. `Invoke` returns the handler's exception to `SingleInstanceHelpers.WaitForClientConnectionsAsync`, which runs the listener. That exception ends the loop. Since the listener task is never awaited, the error is not reported and no listener remains for later launches. ## Proposed changes - In `WindowsFormsApplicationBase.vb`, catch exceptions inside the delegate running on the UI thread and send them to `Application.OnThreadException`. This follows the same route as a `Click` handler exception: it raises `UnhandledException` when handled by the app, or displays the standard dialog otherwise. Dispatch remains synchronous. - In `SingleInstanceHelpers.vb`, keep the listener loop running if its callback throws, as a second safeguard. - Remove the comment that said exceptions from the handler should propagate. - Do not use `BeginInvoke`: before startup completes, the captured context can be the default `SynchronizationContext`, whose `Post` dispatches to a thread-pool thread. An unhandled exception there could terminate the process. ## Customer Impact An exception in `StartupNextInstance` is now handled like another UI exception, while the single-instance listener continues accepting launches. If the app's `UnhandledException` handler leaves `ExitApplication = True` (the default), the app exits, as it would for any other unhandled UI exception. ## Regression? No. The code has been unchanged since at least release/10.0. .NET Framework behavior was not verified. ## Risk Low. Only exception handling changes; normal next-instance handling is unchanged. ## Screenshots ### Before On the shipped .NET 10 runtime, the missing file is not reported and the following launch fails after about 2.6 seconds. ### After The repro displays a blue "Error reported to the app: FileNotFoundException ..." row, and the next launch opens `sample.txt`. ## Test methodology - Unit test `SingleInstanceTests.CallbackThrows_ServerKeepsAcceptingClients`: the callback throws for the first launch, and the second launch must still arrive. Without the fix the second send times out; with it the test passes. - Existing suites pass on this branch: `Microsoft.VisualBasic.Tests` `SingleInstanceTests` (11/11), and `Microsoft.VisualBasic.Forms.Tests` `WindowsFormsApplicationBaseTests` plus `SingleInstanceHelpersTests` (16/16). ## Test environment(s) 12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102 ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15318)

Issues.Title: One exception in a StartupNextInstance handler breaks single instance until the app is closed
Issues.Body: ### .NET version .NET 10 runtime, Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 10.0.14 ### Did it work in .NET Framework? Not tested/verified ### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+? _No response_ ### Issue description When the app is already open and you start it again, the new process does not open a second window. It sends its command-line arguments to the running window through a named pipe, then exits. The running window raises its `StartupNextInstance` event with those arguments. A file viewer might open a command-line file in its `StartupNextInstance` handler by calling `File.ReadAllText`. If the file does not exist, that call throws `FileNotFoundException`. The exception is not reported: `UnhandledException` does not run, and no error dialog appears. The running app also stops accepting launches. Each later launch waits about 2.5 seconds and then fails with `CantStartSingleInstanceException`, until the first instance closes. The exception should reach `UnhandledException` or the standard WinForms dialog, and later launches should still open their files. ### Steps to reproduce The attached minimal repro is a one-file VB app called "single-instance file viewer": 1. Run the app. 2. Click **Open sample.txt**. The file opens and the status is green. 3. Click **Open missing.txt (does not exist)**. The log shows that the path arrived, but there is no further response or error. 4. Click **Open sample.txt** again. About 2.5 seconds later, the log reports "Launch # 3 never reached this window ... CantStartSingleInstanceException" and the verdict turns red. Equivalent repro in any VB app: enable **Make single instance application**, call `File.ReadAllText(e.CommandLine(0))` from `StartupNextInstance`, start the app, launch it with a nonexistent path, then launch it a third time with a valid path. [ReproSingleInstance.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34044933/ReproSingleInstance.zip)

Issues.Title: Use product targeting pack for analyzer tests and add compatibility tests
Issues.Body:
This pull request refactors how the analyzer tests resolve and use .NET reference assemblies, simplifying the logic for determining the correct targeting pack and removing now-unnecessary code. The changes ensure that the analyzer tests always use the repository's configured targeting pack, and update the test coverage accordingly.

**Reference assembly resolution improvements:**

* Refactored `CurrentReferences` to resolve the product's targeting pack directly from the test runtime configuration, removing dependency on the SDK's bundled pack and eliminating logic that searched for or validated the SDK version and available targeting packs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-68fdfe67dd3622ab550b7597c4030dff9c1b3427a66ace8ab5cd763ee2647a3bL45-R51) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-68fdfe67dd3622ab550b7597c4030dff9c1b3427a66ace8ab5cd763ee2647a3bL61-L102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-68fdfe67dd3622ab550b7597c4030dff9c1b3427a66ace8ab5cd763ee2647a3bL113-R98) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-68fdfe67dd3622ab550b7597c4030dff9c1b3427a66ace8ab5cd763ee2647a3bL159-L168)

**Test updates and enhancements:**

* Removed tests related to the old targeting pack resolution logic, and introduced new tests to verify that the analyzer tests use the correct targeting pack and can compile with the resolved references for both C# and Visual Basic.

**General cleanup:**

* Updated comments and documentation to clarify that the tests now use the repository's configured targeting pack, not the SDK's runtime reference pack.

Issues.Title: Enhance ARM64 build scripts and architecture handling
Issues.Body:
This pull request introduces robust support for Windows x64 and ARM64 builds, improving how the repository handles SDK and runtime architecture isolation, installation, and repair. The changes ensure that builds and restores work seamlessly across architectures, correctly manage mixed or reused SDK installations, and provide new scripts and documentation to clarify and automate these processes. The update also adds regression tests to verify architecture handling in CI.

**Build and architecture handling improvements:**

* Added `eng/dotnet-architecture.ps1`, a comprehensive script for detecting, installing, and repairing .NET SDK and runtime installations across x64, ARM64, and x86 architectures, including logic for handling reused or mixed-architecture SDKs and preserving incomplete/incompatible runtimes (`eng/dotnet-architecture.ps1`).
* Updated `eng/configure-toolset.ps1` to use the new architecture detection and repair logic, ensuring that SDK installations match the host or specified architecture and are repaired as needed.
* Added `eng/install-runtimes.ps1`, which installs required .NET runtimes for the correct architecture(s) and ensures all runtime files are present and compatible.
* Introduced `eng/Tools.props` to bypass default Arcade SDK cache checks and invoke the repository’s own runtime installer, ensuring correct runtime isolation and installation for WinForms projects.

**Build script and pipeline updates:**

* Replaced calls to Arcade’s `Build.ps1` with a new `eng/build.cmd.ps1` script in both `build.cmd` and `Restore.cmd`, which parses arguments, sets architecture defaults, and invokes the build with the correct configuration [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5d1a8c1f0cf259b0ef0ad38234ee6760764b2eb416f063f62bb7e54bf84d03c7L2-R2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-112f11a68cd3e870f190282a5cfbbc7627b88ed4e924b7a986f9c7ee84e2d35fL2-R3) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fa2f4f14ee341bb8157431957ebd2cd098b47c8312734a75ad1ee11ff4a6cc98R1-R86).
* Updated `Directory.Build.props` to set the `TargetArchitecture` property based on platform and OS, ensuring builds default to the correct architecture unless explicitly overridden.

**Documentation and CI enhancements:**

* Expanded `docs/building.md` with detailed guidance on Windows x64 and ARM64 builds, SDK/runtime installation behavior, and troubleshooting for mixed-architecture environments.
* Added CI steps in `eng/pipelines/build-PR.yml` to run new regression tests that verify proper SDK and runtime architecture isolation.

These changes collectively improve cross-architecture support, reliability, and clarity for developers working with Windows .NET builds.<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Branch [release/9.0](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/commits/release/9.0/) in `dotnet/winforms` repo can't be mirrored from GitHub to Azure [internal/release/9.0](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-winforms?version=GBinternal%2Frelease%2F9.0&_a=history) via internal merge. 

There are conflicting commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via automated merge. 
The situation is rare but normal. The target branch is expected to receive manual commits in the Azure DevOps clone, which could cause conflict.

Conflicts need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

- you can resolve the issue by resolving the conflict in the **target branch only**. 
    - Please make sure that the changes sensitive from security perspective are not published ahead of time to GitHub!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the conflict is resolved.

Issues.Title: Fix safe publication of the Control callback queue
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15308

## Root cause
The callback queue is lazily initialized under an instance lock, but readers access the queue reference without acquiring that initialization lock. Consequently, the initialization lock alone does not establish safe publication to those readers.

Additionally, the disposal path reads the queue's Count outside the queue lock, even though other threads may modify the queue.

## Proposed change

- Add `volatile` to the callback queue field so other threads can safely access the initialized queue
- Remove the queue-count check outside the lock, the count is already checked inside the lock


<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- Addresses a potential concurrency issue when marshaling callbacks to the UI thread

## Regression? 

- No

## Risk

- Minimal

- .net 12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102

Issues.Title: missing lock in Control.InvokeMarshaledCallbacks
Issues.Body:
### .NET version

.Net 10

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

Not tested/verified

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

Haven't checked.

### Issue description

Control.InvokeMarshaledCallbacks() begins with `if (_threadCallbackList is not null)`. This member is initialized from `MarshaledInvoke(Control caller, Delegate method, object?[]? args, bool synchronous)` which is meant to be called from other threads, so InvokeMarshaledCallbacks should not look at it without synchronization (I mean looking at the field, not the pointed object which is correctly performed inside a lock).

In `MarshaledInvoke`, `_threadCallbackList` is initialized while locking `this`, so I think `Control.InvokeMarshaledCallbacks` should do the same (alternately, one could just initialize it from the constructor and get rid of the `lock(this)`; would the extra memory usage be that terrible?). 

TBH, I'm not sure there can be really bad consequences, but better safe than sorry.  Probably the worst realistic scenario is that the invoke won't be performed until the next call to `InvokeMarshaledCallbacks`. But one could imagine that a very aggressive JIT compiler would realize that `_threadCallbackList` is never assigned from the UI thread, and decide that all the code in the function can be elided.

### Steps to reproduce

As discussed above, there is no visible bug.

Issues.Title: DataGridView lacks a reliable “binding settled” event after DataSource assignment
Issues.Body:
I observed that assigning a DataTable to DataGridView.DataSource may trigger multiple internal event cycles for a single binding operation.

The following events can fire repeatedly:
- SelectionChanged
- RowEnter
- CellEnter
- DataBindingComplete

This occurs even when DataSource is assigned only once.

Business workflows often require cascading data loading after a grid is ready.
For example:
Load Test List    ->   Load Parameter    ->   Load Calibration    ->   Load QC

Because DataBindingComplete may fire multiple times and SelectionChanged may occur repeatedly during binding, application code must implement custom debounce logic using BeginInvoke, version tokens, timers, or other workarounds.

A dedicated "Ready" or "BindingSettled" event would significantly simplify DataGridView usage.

Test code VB.NET:

Dim dt As DataTable = GetAllTestName()
   Log("START BIND")
   dgvTestName.DataSource = dt
   Log("END BIND")

Log result:

START BIND

RowEnter
CellEnter
SelectionChanged
DataBindingComplete

SelectionChanged
RowEnter
CellEnter
SelectionChanged
DataBindingComplete

END BIND

SelectionChanged
RowEnter
CellEnter
SelectionChanged
DataBindingComplete

(repeated multiple times)

Issues.Title: Fix issue 15295: Reentrency issue in ToolStripManager.ProcessShortcut in presence of a dynamic context menu
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15295 

## Root Cause

PR #10291 changed ToolStripManager.ProcessShortcut from index-based iteration to foreach over WeakRefCollection<ToolStrip>.

During iteration, ProcessShortcut repeatedly accessed the overridable ContextMenuStrip property. Applications with dynamically generated context menus may add or dispose ToolStrip instances from this getter, modifying the underlying collection. The foreach enumerator then detected the modification and threw InvalidOperationException.

## Proposed changes

Cache each control's ContextMenuStrip value once before enumerating registered ToolStrip instances. Reuse the cached active-control context menu throughout shortcut resolution.

This prevents reentrant collection modification during enumeration, avoids repeated invocation of potentially expensive overridden getters, and preserves existing shortcut-routing behavior. A regression test covers a getter that modifies the active ToolStrip collection.

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

Applications using dynamically generated context menus can crash when processing keyboard shortcuts, even when the pressed shortcut is not present in the menu.

The issue affects applications whose overridden ContextMenuStrip getter creates or disposes ToolStrip objects. It is expected to affect .NET 9 and later; .NET 8 and .NET Framework retain the previous non-fail-fast iteration behavior.


## Regression? 

- Yes

## Risk

- Mini

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Fix issue 14449: ToolStrip DPI change issue in .NET 10
Issues.Body:
Backport of #14454 to release/10.0

Fixes #14449 

This issue was introduced by PR [#13582](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/13582), when we drag the ToolStrip control on screens with different DPI settings, the call stack history is [WmDpiChangedBeforeParent](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/5d71425a3fecf8f72a57679b53bd2b5035ca0059/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Control.cs#L11562) -> [RescaleConstantsForDpi](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/5d71425a3fecf8f72a57679b53bd2b5035ca0059/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Controls/ToolStrips/ToolStrip.cs#L3725). However, within the WmDpiChangedBeforeParent method, [OriginalDeviceDpiInternal](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/blob/5d71425a3fecf8f72a57679b53bd2b5035ca0059/src/System.Windows.Forms/System/Windows/Forms/Control.cs#L470-L475) and DeviceDpiInternal retrieve the same value, which will cause the RescaleConstantsForDpi method in the ToolStrip class to fail to execute as expected.

## Proposed changes

-  OriginalDeviceDpiInternal = DeviceDpiInternal; is effectively a no-op in the common case: the setter uses DeviceDpiInternal as the default value to remove the stored property, so after DeviceDpiInternal is updated later in this method, OriginalDeviceDpiInternal will again resolve to the new DPI. This means other code that relies on OriginalDeviceDpiInternal != DeviceDpiInternal during/after the DPI-change path will still observe them as equal. So consider capturing oldDeviceDpi first, updating DeviceDpiInternal to the new DPI, and then assigning OriginalDeviceDpiInternal = oldDeviceDpi so it is persisted (mirroring how Form sets OriginalDeviceDpiInternal = e.DeviceDpiOld).

<!-- We are in TELL-MODE the following section must be completed -->

## Customer Impact

- ToolStrip DPI change correctly in .NET 10.

## Regression? 

- Yes- regression PR https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/13582.

## Testing

- Manually
- Unit test

## Risk

- Minimal
